title: Binary derived open descent for modules on a ringed topos
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a Grothendieck topos (a category of sheaves of sets on a small site), $R$ a commutative ring object of $\mathcal T$, and $D(\mathcal T,R)$ the ordinary derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ be subterminal objects (monomorphisms into the terminal object) whose union is $1$, and put $W=U\times V$. Write $\mathcal T/U$, $\mathcal T/V$, $\mathcal T/W$ for the slice topoi, $R_U,R_V,R_W$ for the restricted rings, and $j_Z^*$ for restriction to a slice. The exact extension-by-zero left adjoint is denoted $j_{Z!}$ and the derived right adjoint of restriction is denoted $Rj_{Z*}$, for $Z=U,V,W$.

(1) Given $A\in D(\mathcal T/U,R_U)$, $B\in D(\mathcal T/V,R_V)$ and an isomorphism $c:A|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}B|_W$, there exist $G\in D(\mathcal T,R)$ and isomorphisms $a:G|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, $b:G|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $b|_W=c\circ a|_W$. One may take $G$ in a distinguished triangle
$$G\longrightarrow Rj_{U*}A\oplus Rj_{V*}B\xrightarrow{(Rj_*c,-1)}Rj_{W*}(B|_W)\longrightarrow G[1],$$
where each component is the derived restriction-adjunction map, with $c$ applied in the first component. If $A,B$ have cohomology in a common interval $[a_0,b_0]$, so does $G$.

(2) For every $M\in D(\mathcal T,R)$ there is the natural distinguished open-cover triangle
$$j_{W!}(M|_W)\xrightarrow{(1,-1)}j_{U!}(M|_U)\oplus j_{V!}(M|_V)\xrightarrow{(1,1)}M\longrightarrow j_{W!}(M|_W)[1].$$
The arrows are the canonical nested-open maps and the adjunction counits. Restriction and extension by zero here act termwise on complexes. No uniqueness of a gluing of arbitrary derived morphisms is asserted.

proof.text: Use the simultaneous presentation and module equivalences in [lem-sp-binary-cover-site-presentation]. We may work on its small site and the $U,V,W$ slices, with all adjunction maps identified. The exact restriction, extension and local vanishing tests are [lem-sp-subterminal-module-local-calculus]; the right-image comparisons, including their units and counits, are [lem-sp-subterminal-derived-image-calculus].

Put $D=B|_W$. Define $r_A,r_B$ by the normalized adjunction maps of [lem-sp-subterminal-derived-image-calculus] and $d=(Rj_{W*}(c)r_A,-r_B)$. Complete $d$ to a fibre triangle $G\xrightarrow fRj_{U*}A\oplus Rj_{V*}B\xrightarrow dRj_{W*}D\to G[1]$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On $U$ its middle arrow is $(h,-1)$ with $h=Rk_{U*}(c)\eta_A$; on $V$, after identifying the first summand by $Rk_{V*}(c)$, it is $(1,-\eta_B)$. By [lem-sp-derived-split-fibre-projections], the restrict-project-counit maps $a:G|_U\to A$ and $b:G|_V\to B$ are isomorphisms. On $W$ the arrow is $(c,-1)$, so $df=0$ says $c\,a|_W=b|_W$.

If $q\notin[a_0,b_0]$, exact restriction and $a,b$ give $H^q(G)|_U=H^q(A)=0$ and $H^q(G)|_V=H^q(B)=0$. Joint zero detection in [lem-sp-subterminal-module-local-calculus] gives $H^q(G)=0$. Thus the same $G$ has every common interval bound; no bound on intermediate direct images is used.

For a complex $K$ representing $M$, [lem-sp-subterminal-cover-module-ses] gives the natural degreewise short exact sequence with arrows $(i_U,-i_V)$ and $(\epsilon_U,\epsilon_V)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to obtain its distinguished triangle and natural connecting map. The termwise exact functors of [lem-sp-subterminal-module-local-calculus] identify its vertices and arrows with those in (2). Naturality descends from complexes to the derived localization: the exact functors invert quasi-isomorphisms, and the naturality square for an inverse follows by inverting its sides. This yields one natural connecting transformation for all $M$. Finally the equivalences of [lem-sp-binary-cover-site-presentation] return both constructions and their canonical arrows to $\mathcal T$.
